clue.text: Not easily broken idols

indicators.note: idols that are broken are smashed into pieces, so their letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Graven images that resist all attempts to smash them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' does double service in this old-style clue: it is the anagram signal on IDOLS, and the whole clue reads as a description of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sturdy and firm, hard to shatter, is described as solid.

clue.text: Disapproval is audibly ex pressed -in them

definitions.text: Disapproval is audibly ex pressed -in them

parts.words: Disapproval is audibly ex pressed -in them
parts.note: booing or hissing an act is spoken disapproval, and a hiss is made of the s-sounds of speech

explanation.surface: Sounds an audience uses to show it dislikes a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: A hiss of disapproval is pure s-sound, the very speech sound that phoneticians name by this term.
explanation.definitionFit: Hissing consonants such as s and sh are the phonetic class named here, the sounds in which a hiss is voiced.

clue.text: It can't help being grubby

parts.note: grubby is read literally as being in the form of a grub, the young stage of an insect

explanation.surface: Something that is dirty through no fault of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grubby' looks like dirty, but it means grub-like: an insect cannot help passing through its grub stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's young wormlike stage after hatching, a grub or caterpillar, is this term.

clue.text: Creating these. records, is an everyday occurrence

definitions.text: Creating these. records, is an everyday occurrence

parts.words: Creating these. records, is an everyday occurrence
parts.note: an everyday occurrence is read literally as an entry made each day, the way a journal is kept

explanation.surface: Keeping records is routine business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an everyday occurrence' sounds like something commonplace, but it describes writing a day-by-day log.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal journals in which entries are made each day are these books.

clue.text: To which intelligent women have Shavian guidance

definitions.text: To which intelligent women have Shavian guidance

parts.words: To which intelligent women have Shavian guidance
parts.note: George Bernard Shaw wrote a book titled The Intelligent Woman's Guide to this political creed and capitalism

explanation.surface: Advice from Bernard Shaw for clever women.
explanation.walkthrough: Shavian means of George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright, whose 1928 book was a guide for the intelligent woman to this political doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: The political theory of common ownership of the means of production, which Shaw championed as a Fabian.

clue.text: Their deficiencies made up in a roundabout, way'?

definitions.text: Their deficiencies made up in a roundabout, way'?

parts.words: Their deficiencies made up in a roundabout, way'?
parts.note: the saying goes that what you lose on these playground rides you gain on the roundabouts

explanation.surface: Shortfalls compensated for indirectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' looks like 'indirect', but it is the fairground ride in the proverb about losses on one side balanced by gains on the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Playground seats hung on chains or ropes for rocking back and forth, paired in the proverb with roundabouts (merry-go-rounds).

clue.text: With others he swears-to do the hat-trick ?

definitions.meaning: an old sense of the word is one who is sworn together with others in a conspiracy, as CON- (with) plus JUROR suggests
the magician's trick of pulling a rabbit from a hat

explanation.surface: A man who takes an oath alongside others before pulling off a triple feat.
explanation.walkthrough: The hat-trick looks like three goals or wickets, but it is the magician's rabbit from a top hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician performs illusions, and the archaic sense is a fellow oath-taker in a plot.

clue.text: She takes a month to reach a conclusion

indicators.note: the month reaches an A as its conclusion, so A follows it

parts.note: the eighth month of the year

explanation.surface: A woman who needs four weeks to come to a decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reach a conclusion' sounds like deciding, but it says the month gets A at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, as in Augusta Ada Lovelace.

clue.text: State of the people of Nuneaton ?

definitions.text: State of the people of Nuneaton ?

parts.words: State of the people of Nuneaton ?
parts.note: the town name Nuneaton is read as 'none eaten', and people who have eaten nothing are weak from hunger

explanation.surface: A question about the condition of residents of a Warwickshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Nuneaton is a town in Warwickshire, England; read as 'none eaten' it describes starvation.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term for exhaustion caused by lack of nourishment.

clue.text: Author of two generations

parts.note: a mother is one generation
a son is the generation after

explanation.surface: A writer whose family spans parent and child.
explanation.definitionFit: A.E.W. Mason was an English novelist, author of The Four Feathers.

clue.text: A Scot is twice barred — for being rude?

indicators.note: the word meaning barred is used two times over

parts.note: to bar is to ban or shut out
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman excluded two times because of his bad manners.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian is the Scottish form of John, so it stands for any Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, it means uncivilised or uncouth, like an uncultured outsider.

clue.text: Net results of good shooting

parts.note: net results looks like profit after costs, but it means balls ending in the net after accurate shots

explanation.surface: The final profit earned from a successful hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net results' sounds like accounts, but in football the ball shot well ends in the net.
explanation.definitionFit: Successful shots in football or hockey that cross the line into the net are scored as these.

clue.text: It-should bring the following answer

parts.note: a barrister's prompt that guides a witness to a reply already in mind

explanation.surface: A query designed to produce the response that comes next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the following answer' reads like the next entry, but it is the reply the questioner wants to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: In court, a prompt phrased to suggest the reply it wants is objected to as this kind of query.

clue.text: Underworld chief among numbers in health movement

indicators.note: the underworld ruler is placed among, so within, the letters for numbers

parts.note: Num. abbreviates Numbers, the fourth book of the Bible
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld

explanation.surface: The ruler of Hades mixing with crowds in a fitness campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Num. is the standard abbreviation for the Old Testament book Numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturism, going unclothed, was promoted as a healthy way of life.

clue.text: It's a command, in a way

definitions.meaning: a route or course to follow

explanation.definitionFit: An instruction is an order given, and a compass bearing or route is a way to go.

clue.text: She's one to put Lord's in a turmoil

indicators.note: being put in a turmoil throws things into confusion, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the possessive keeps its S here as a letter of the fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman who would cause chaos at the London cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground; its letters with IN A are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, borne by the heroine of Shakespeare's As You Like It.

clue.text: Preparations for dinner-in more than one senses

definitions.text: Preparations for dinner-in more than one senses

parts.words: Preparations for dinner-in more than one senses
parts.note: getting into evening clothes, and making salad sauces, are both readying for a meal

explanation.surface: Getting ready for an evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Changing into formal clothes and mixing sauces for salad are both ways to prepare for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauces for salad, and putting on formal clothes, are both senses of this word.

clue.text: Homer apt to misuse this figure of speech ?

indicators.note: to misuse words is to mangle them, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Would the Greek poet use this literary device badly?
explanation.walkthrough: Homer looks like the poet, but his name is just letters to rearrange with APT.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech describing one thing as another, without 'like' or 'as'.

clue.text: One who approaches 12 by degrees

parts.note: 12 across is the creed of going unclothed, approached gradually by shedding garments one at a time

explanation.surface: Someone who gradually works towards a health movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 across is the movement for going without clothes; this performer gets there one garment at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque performer who removes clothing piece by piece for an audience.

clue.text: Course of action

definitions.meaning: a series of steps or a method
a legal case or summons in court

explanation.definitionFit: A method is a series of steps, and in law a lawsuit or writ is legal action of this kind.

clue.text: Even the most uninterested find it absorbing

definitions.text: Even the most uninterested find it absorbing

parts.words: Even the most uninterested find it absorbing
parts.note: absorbing is read literally as soaking up liquid, which this bath item does regardless of interest

explanation.surface: Something gripping to the most bored of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' looks like fascinating, but it means soaking up water.
explanation.definitionFit: A porous bath item that soaks up water, also the sea creature that yields it.

clue.text: Foreshadow the last of the wine

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: Predicting that a bottle is almost finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To be an omen of something to come is to presage or signal it.

clue.text: Word of more than one meaning

definitions.text: Word of more than one meaning

parts.words: Word of more than one meaning
parts.note: looks like an ambiguous term, but it is a grammatical form meaning more than one thing

explanation.surface: A term with several senses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of more than one meaning' looks like ambiguity, but it is a word whose meaning is more than one.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical form denoting several things, as 'cats' rather than 'cat'.

clue.text: Proverbially, not a master mariner !

parts.note: the proverb says this handyman is master of none, and a jack is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor who never made captain, as the saying goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb ends 'master of none'; a jack (tar) is an old word for a sailor, hence mariner.
explanation.definitionFit: A handyman able to turn a hand to anything, master of none according to the saying.

clue.text: King Henry as author

definitions.meaning: the name of several kings of England and Scotland

explanation.definitionFit: Several British monarchs, such as the one behind the King James Bible, bore this name, as did the novelist of The Turn of the Screw.

clue.text: Unquestionably there is none

parts.note: the phrase 'without question' implies no uncertainty, as in the idiom 'no ...'

explanation.surface: Certainly nothing is there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unquestionably' is the same as saying there is 'no' of this.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncertainty or misgiving, which is absent when something is beyond question.

clue.text: Chief 13 in New England

parts.note: main means principal
13 down is a compass bearing, and E is east

explanation.surface: The principal route to New England.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 refers to the clue 13 down; E for east is one such bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The north-easternmost US state, one of the six making up New England.

clue.text: Colourful pantomime character

parts.note: the masked clown of the commedia dell'arte, in a diamond-patterned suit

explanation.surface: A brightly dressed figure in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pantomime, the Christmas stage show, this figure in a chequered motley suit was a stock character.
explanation.definitionFit: The motley-suited clown and lover of Columbine in the traditional harlequinade.

clue.text: Inclined to go left

parts.note: inclined is read as leaning or tending, so leaning towards the left-hand side

explanation.surface: Tending towards the political left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go left' suggests politics, but this word means left-handed or spiralling to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: Left-handed, or turning leftward, from the Latin for left.

clue.text: Reveals age of fruit

definitions.meaning: to establish how old something is
the sweet brown fruit of a palm

explanation.surface: Shows how old some produce is.
explanation.definitionFit: To find the period of an object, and the sticky fruits of the palm tree.
